expectations.text: Advises starting coarser / not pre-splitting the three phases into many files up front
expectations.evidence: "start coarser than your instinct probably tells you"; "resist the urge to add types.ts, constants.ts, utils.ts barrels up front"; explicitly warns against pre-splitting the job into enqueue.ts/runner.ts/writer.ts.

expectations.text: Co-locates tightly coupled job lifecycle / polling
expectations.evidence: "The job lifecycle is tightly coupled — co-locate it." Keeps enqueue/run/write-status in one export-job.ts; client trigger+poll pushed into one use-export() hook rather than split.

expectations.text: Recommends an abstraction (function/module) over bare file splits
expectations.evidence: "prefer a hook over splitting UI from logic" — useExport() that hides state; "That's a real abstraction reducing context, not just relocated code."

expectations.text: Mentions a ~300-line threshold (or 'a few hundred lines') as the split trigger
expectations.evidence: "Only split when it crosses ~300 lines or genuinely splits into separate concerns."
